paper_title: Artifact Evaluation for [OOPSLA'26] Automatically Generating ML Compiler Backends from Tensor Accelerator ISA Descriptions
readme:
# ACT: Automatically Generating Compiler Backends from Tensor Accelerator ISA Descriptions

This is the artifact for our paper on automatically generating sound and complete compiler backends for tensor accelerators from their ISA descriptions written in TAIDL.

This artifact consists of ACT source code, TAIDL ISA definitions, input kernel benchmarks, and the necessary scripts to reproduce the evaluation results.
To facilitate artifact evaluation, we have automated the entire environment setup and experimental processes as part of Docker images.

## System Requirements

**Docker**

We use Docker images for environment setup of ACT and baselines.
To run the ACT artifact, install Docker using the [installation guide](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/).

**Architecture Support**

- **amd64/x86_64** is fully supported.
- On **arm64**, the ACT image and Steps 0-1 work; Step 2 requires amd64 due to baseline dependencies (e.g., Gemmini, Chipyard) that are not available for arm64.

## ACT Artifact Overview

### Scripts

The `scripts/` directory contains the following bash scripts to automate the experimental workflows:

- `setup.sh` - pull the ACT Docker image from Docker Hub, or build either image locally.
- `kick-tires.sh` - compile the QKV running example end to end and regenerate all paper figures from the paper's benchmarking data.
- `full.sh` - run ACT compiler backends on every benchmark kernel along with the baselines.
- `clean.sh` - remove all files generated including the log files and PDF plots.

### Docker Images

| Docker image                                      | Environment installed                                                                                    | Architecture | Dockerfile                               |
| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| `devanshdvj/act-oopsla26-artifact:amd64`          | ACT (Rust, OR-Tools, Python) and the plotting toolchain                                                  | amd64        | `docker/artifact-act/Dockerfile.amd64` |
| `devanshdvj/act-oopsla26-artifact:arm64`          | ACT (Rust, OR-Tools, Python) and the plotting toolchain                                                  | arm64        | `docker/artifact-act/Dockerfile.arm64` |
| `devanshdvj/act-oopsla26-artifact:baseline-amd64` | Everything in the ACT image, plus Gemmini RTL simulation (Chipyard, Verilator) and the AWS NKI simulator | amd64        | `docker/artifact-baseline/Dockerfile`  |

The ACT image is pulled from Docker Hub and is all that Step 1 needs.
The baseline image is the complete evaluation environment used by Step 2.

### Generated PDF Plots and CSV Data Files

`plots/paper_data/` contains the paper's benchmarking data as CSV, and is where the figures are written.

Figures:

- `perf-summary.pdf` - Figure 20: compilation coverage for AWS NKI, and geomean speedup of the compiled code
- `perf-gemmini.pdf` - Figure 21: speedup of ACT-Gemmini over the Exo library and over the Gemmini SW library
- `compilation_time.pdf` - Figure 23: breakdown of compilation time for ACT-Gemmini and ACT-NKI
- `perf-gemmini-appendix.pdf` - Appendix G: speedup over the Gemmini SW library, and relative data movement

Tables:

- `nki_coverage.csv` - Per-kernel compilation status and speedup for the TPUGraphs kernels
- `gemmini_exo_perf.csv` - Appendix F: cycle counts for every loop-fission factor of the six Exo GEMM shapes
- `gemmini_swlib_perf.csv` - Cycle counts of ACT-Gemmini and the Gemmini SW library, per kernel
- `amx_perf.csv` - Per-kernel speedup of ACT-AMX over the oneDNN library
- `gemmini_fuzz_compile.csv`, `nki_stress_compile.csv` - Raw data for the compilation time figure
- `gemmini_data_movement.csv` - Scratchpad traffic in bytes for the composite kernels

## Step-by-Step Instructions to Reproduce Results

### (Step 0) Setup the Docker Environment

This will pull the ACT Docker image from Docker Hub.
This should only take a few minutes.

Run the setup script using:

```bash
./scripts/setup.sh
```

Alternatively, you can build the image locally using:

```bash
./scripts/setup.sh --build
```

### (Step 1) Kick the Tires: QKV End-to-End and Quick Plot Generation

This generates the QKV compiler backend from its TAIDL ISA specification, builds it, and compiles the QKV attention kernel to accelerator assembly.
It then uses the paper's benchmarking data (`plots/paper_data/`) to regenerate all figures.
This should only take a few minutes to run.

Run the kick-tires script using:

```bash
./scripts/kick-tires.sh
```

Outputs:

- `compiled_asm/qkv/qkv.asm.py` - QKV accelerator assembly emitted by ACT
- `plots/paper_data/*.pdf` - all paper figures, redrawn from the paper's benchmarking data

### (Step 2) Full Evaluation with Baselines

This step needs the baseline image (`baseline-amd64`), which adds the Gemmini RTL simulator (Chipyard, Verilator) and the AWS NKI simulator on top of the ACT toolchain.
It is pulled or built from `docker/artifact-baseline/Dockerfile`, and is set up once and reused:

```bash
./scripts/setup.sh --full
```

Building it locally (`--full --build`) compiles Chipyard, the RISC-V toolchain, and Verilator from source.
It can take a few hours depending on the machine, and needs at least 60 GB of free disk.

`full.sh` then generates every compiler backend from its TAIDL ISA specification, compiles all benchmark kernels, and measures the compiled code against the baselines.

Run the full script using:

```bash
./scripts/full.sh
```

A default run takes under ten minutes and prints a stage summary when it finishes.
Most of it is ACT-Gemmini (115 kernels compiled and 30 RTL simulations, about 4 minutes) and ACT-NKI (1055 kernels compiled and validated, about 3 minutes).

For every full run, a new folder is created as `plots/full_run_<timestamp>/` containing the generated PDF plots and CSV data files.
The tables in `plots/paper_data/` are copied into that folder and the measured rows are updated there, so the paper's data is left untouched.

Three stages are long enough to be opt-in:

```bash
./scripts/full.sh --regen-kernels       # also regenerate the TPUGraphs and NNSmith kernels (five minutes)
./scripts/full.sh --rerun-neuronxcc     # also recompile the TPUGraphs kernels with neuronx-cc (doubles the NKI stage)
./scripts/full.sh --rerun-exo-sweep     # also re-measure all 112 Exo loop-fission variants (more than a day)
```

Pass `-j N` to set the number of parallel simulator jobs; by default it uses all but two of the available cores.

### (Optional) Cleanup/Fresh Start

To remove all generated files including log files and PDF plots, run:

```bash
./scripts/clean.sh
```

## Project Structure

- `act/` - ACT source: the TAIDL ISA language and the backend generator
- `accelerators/` - TAIDL ISA definitions
  - `qkv.py` - QKV ISA (running example in the paper)
  - `gemmini.py` - Gemmini ISA
  - `nki.py` - AWS NKI ISA
  - `scripts/` - Per-accelerator run scripts
- `kernels/` - Input HLO benchmark programs
  - `qkv/` - QKV kernel (running example in the paper)
  - `gemmini/` - Gemmini kernels (SW library and fuzz-generated)
  - `nki/` - AWS Trainium kernels (TPUGraphs)
- `evaluation/` - Per-accelerator evaluation harnesses
- `docker/artifact-act/` - ACT compilation and plotting Docker environment
- `docker/artifact-baseline/` - Full evaluation Docker environment (Gemmini RTL simulator and NKI simulator)
- `plots/` - Visualization scripts and paper data
- `scripts/` - Automation scripts

## Key Claims

The evaluation in the paper makes three key claims, and this artifact reproduces all of them.

| Key claim                                                                                                                                               | In the paper          | Reproduced by                   | Output                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **(C1) Compilation coverage.** ACT-NKI correctly compiles all 1055 TPUGraphs kernels, against 459 for `neuronx-cc`.                                     | Figure 20(a)          | Stage (3) of `full.sh`          | `nki_coverage.csv`, `perf-summary.pdf`                                                                 |
| **(C2) Performance improvement.** Code compiled by ACT-Gemmini outperforms the Exo library and the Gemmini SW library, measured in RTL cycles.          | Figure 21, Appendix G | Stage (2) of `full.sh`          | `gemmini_swlib_perf.csv`, `gemmini_data_movement.csv`, `perf-gemmini.pdf`, `perf-gemmini-appendix.pdf` |
| **(C3) Compilation time.** ACT-generated backends compile tiled kernels within seconds, and the per-phase breakdown scales with the size of the kernel. | Figure 23             | Stages (2) and (3) of `full.sh` | `gemmini_fuzz_compile.csv`, `nki_stress_compile.csv`, `compilation_time.pdf`                           |

A single `./scripts/full.sh` run reproduces all three claims and writes every file above to `plots/full_run_<timestamp>/`.

### (C1) Compilation Coverage

Stage (3) compiles all 1055 TPUGraphs kernels in `kernels/nki/tpugraphs/` with the ACT-NKI backend, translates each emitted `asm.py` into NKI, runs it on the AWS NKI simulator, and compares the result against the XLA oracle (`jaxlib.xla_client`).
The stage prints one line per kernel and ends with:

```
Completed the NKI coverage kernels: 1055/1055 validated.
```

Per-kernel results are written to `compiled_asm/nki/coverage_results.log` and folded into `nki_coverage.csv` (`kernel,family,neuronx_cc,act,speedup`).
Panel (a) of `perf-summary.pdf` groups the kernels by workload family, and the run prints the same breakdown:

```
NKI coverage by family (a):
      ResNet Variants         neuronx_cc=87    act=242
      Inception Variants      neuronx_cc=81    act=162
      Object Detection        neuronx_cc=39    act=220
      Other Vision Models     neuronx_cc=39    act=66
      BERT Variants           neuronx_cc=84    act=119
      Transformer Variants    neuronx_cc=123   act=165
      Other ML Workloads      neuronx_cc=6     act=81
      TOTAL                   neuronx_cc=459   act=1055
```

`./scripts/full.sh --rerun-neuronxcc` additionally recompiles the same 1055 kernels with `neuronx-cc` inside the baseline image, which fills the `neuronx_cc` column.

### (C2) Performance Improvement

Stage (2) compiles the 15 tiled kernels in `kernels/gemmini/swlib/`, lowers each emitted `asm.py` into its C scaffold, and runs both the ACT-Gemmini kernel and the Gemmini SW library kernel on the Gemmini RTL simulator (Verilator).
Each run checks its result against a gold value computed in C, and prints its cycle count:

```
[ 1/30] A_plus_B                       | ACT-Gemmini | Cycles:  193 | VALIDATED
[ 2/30] A_plus_B_library               | Library     | Cycles:  192 | VALIDATED
```

The cycle counts land in `gemmini_swlib_perf.csv` (`kernel,class,act_cycles,baseline_cycles`), where `class` is the grouping of Figure 21(b): `supported`, `composite`, or `not supported`.
Scratchpad traffic for the composite kernels lands in `gemmini_data_movement.csv` (`kernel,act_bytes,baseline_bytes`), which is the right panel of `perf-gemmini-appendix.pdf`.

The geomean speedups of the redrawn figure are printed at the end of the run:

```
  ACT-Gemmini vs Exo Library             1.10x
  ACT-Gemmini vs Gemmini SW Library      1.52x
```

Panel (a) of `perf-gemmini.pdf` is drawn from `gemmini_exo_perf.csv`, the cycle counts of all 112 loop-fission variants of the six Exo GEMM shapes.
`./scripts/full.sh --rerun-exo-sweep` re-measures them on Verilator.

### (C3) Compilation Time

Stage (2) also compiles the 100 fuzz kernels in `kernels/gemmini/fuzz/`, and stage (3) the 3 stress kernels in `kernels/nki/stress/`.
Both record the per-phase timings that the backend reports for every kernel.

`gemmini_fuzz_compile.csv` (`nodes,applier,extractor,csp_gen,csp_solve,rest`) bins the kernels by HLO node count in groups of ten, and `nki_stress_compile.csv` keeps one row per kernel.
All timings are in milliseconds; the four phase columns are the rewriter and the extractor of Phase 1, and the CSP generation and the CSP solver of Phase 2.
`compilation_time.pdf` stacks those columns against kernel size, which is Figure 23.

## Reusability Guide

ACT is not tied to the accelerators evaluated in the paper: a new compiler backend is generated from a TAIDL ISA specification alone, with no changes to the compilation algorithm.
`REUSABILITY.md` defines a custom ISA end to end, compiles a kernel with the generated backend, and documents the TAIDL API and the backend command-line interface.
Further tutorials are available in the public ACT repository at [https://github.com/act-compiler/act](https://github.com/act-compiler/act).
